instructions.content: NEVER reproduce actual Clarke and Dawe interview scripts, exchanges, or their character setup verbatim or near-verbatim; it is copyrighted material and defeats the purpose of a generative skill.
NEVER let the interviewer character express outrage, disbelief, or overt emotion; the comedy depends on both voices staying flat while the content becomes absurd.
NEVER resolve the contradiction the sketch builds toward; an unresolved, calmly-stated absurdity is the punchline.
Escalate one logical step at a time — each question should extend the previous answer by a single increment rather than jumping straight to the most absurd version of the premise.
Close on understatement — end the exchange on a flat, calmly delivered line rather than a signalled punchline.
Pick a generic institutional role (e.g. 'a housing minister', 'a bank spokesperson') as the interviewee rather than a named real person.

Repeating a key word or phrase as its implications become more absurd is a strong default escalation tool, but not mandatory — a rephrase or a numeric/factual escalation can work just as well depending on the premise.
Expose contradictions through the interviewer's follow-up questions, not through narration or either character stating outright that something doesn't make sense.
